questions.question: A particle with initial velocity $3\widehat{i} + 4\widehat{j}$ has an acceleration of $0.4\widehat{i} + 0.3\widehat{j}$. Its speed after 10 sec is?
hints: Use $\overrightarrow{v} = \ \overrightarrow{u} + \ \overrightarrow{a}t$

questions.question: Velocity of a particle at time t = 0 is 2 m/s. A constant acceleration of 2 m/$s^{2}$ acts on the particle for 2 seconds at an angle of 60° with its initial velocity. Find the magnitude of velocity and displacement of particle at the end of t = 2 s.
hints:
> Let the initial velocity be $2\widehat{i}$ then acceleration: $\widehat{i} + \sqrt{3}\widehat{j}$

>

> Final velocity: $4\widehat{i} + 2\sqrt{3}\widehat{j}$ Average velocity: 3$\widehat{i} + \sqrt{3}\widehat{j}$

questions.question: A particle moves from the point $\left( 2\widehat{i} + 4\widehat{j} \right)$m, at t = 0 with initial velocity $\left( 5\widehat{i} + 4\widehat{j} \right)ms^{- 1}$. It is acted upon by a constant force which produces a constant acceleration $\left( 4\widehat{i} + 4\widehat{j} \right)ms^{- 2}$. What is the distance of the particle from the origin at time 2 s?

A mosquito is moving with a velocity $\overrightarrow{v} = 0.5t^{2}\widehat{i} + 3t\widehat{j} + 9\widehat{k}\ $m/s and accelerating in uniform conditions. What will be the direction of mosquito after 2 s ?
hints: > $\overrightarrow{v}(2) = 2\widehat{i} + 6\widehat{j} + 9\widehat{k}$ $\tan \alpha(x - axis):\frac{\sqrt{v_{y}^{2} + v_{z}^{2}}}{v_{x}}$

questions.question: A particle at origin is moving with initial velocity $\overrightarrow{u} = 5\ m/s\widehat{j}$ and a constant acceleration $10\widehat{i} + 4\widehat{j}\ m/s^{2}$. At time t, its co-ordinates are $(20\ m,\ y_{0}\ m)$. The value of t and $y_{0}$ respectively are:

hints: > Will reach maximum x co-ordinate when $v_{x} = 0$ (at t = 3 s)

The position vector of a particle is given as $\overrightarrow{r} = \left( t^{2} - 4t + 6 \right)\widehat{i} + (t^{2})\widehat{j}$. The time ‘t’ when the velocity vector and acceleration vector become perpendicular to each other is?
hints:
> $\overrightarrow{v} = (2t - 4)\widehat{i} + (2t)\widehat{j}$ $\overrightarrow{a} = 2\widehat{i} + 2\widehat{j}$

>

> Mutually perpendicular when the dot product is zero

questions.question: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 with a velocity of $\overrightarrow{u} = 8\widehat{j}$ m/s and moves in the xy plane with a constant acceleration of $\overrightarrow{a} = 4\widehat{i} + 2\widehat{j}$ m/s<sup>2</sup>. At the instant the particle’s x–coordinate is 32 m, what are (i) its y–coordinate and (ii) its speed?

A body of mass 2 kg moves under a force of 2$\widehat{i} + 3\widehat{j} + 5\widehat{k}N$. It starts from rest and was at the origin initially. After 4 s, its new coordinates are (8, b, 20). The value of b is _____(Round off to the nearest Integer)
The co-ordinates of a particle moving in x-y plane at any time t are (2t, t<sup>2</sup>). Find (i) the trajectory of the particle (ii) velocity of particle at time t?
A particle moves in space along the path $z = ax^{3} + by^{2}$ in such a way that $\frac{dx}{dt} = c = \frac{dy}{dt};\ $ where a, b and c are constants. The acceleration of the particle is?
hints:
> X and Y components of acceleration are zero.

>

> $\frac{dz}{dt} = 3ax^{2}\left( \frac{dx}{dt} \right) + 2by\left( \frac{dy}{dt} \right) = 3acx^{2} + 2bcy$; then differentiate again

>

> As it makes an angle of $30{^\circ}$ with the horizontal $u_{x} = 10\sqrt{3}$

>

> Two seconds prior to this, the y-component of velocity will be: 30 m/s

questions.question: A particle is projected from the ground with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° with horizontal. The magnitude of change in velocity in 0.5 second is:

questions.question: An oblique projectile on a horizontal plane has a range of 105 m and has a time of flight of 7 sec. Find the displacement of the projectile in the 4<sup>th</sup> second of its motion.
hints:
> The projectile will be at the same height at 3 s and 4 s (as it reaches the highest point at time 3.5 s)

>

> Hence the displacement = horizontal distance travelled = $u_{x} = \frac{105}{7} = 15m$

questions.question: The horizontal range and maximum height attained by a projectile are R = 90 m and H = 45 m respectively. If a constant horizontal acceleration a = g/10 is imparted to the projectile due to wind in the direction of its horizontal component of motion, then its horizontal range and maximum height will be?
questions.conventional:
> The original time of flight is 6 s (as $H = 45m)$; hence $u_{x} = 15$ m/s

>

> The horizontal acceleration will not change time of flight or the maximum height.

>

> Horizontal displacement with $a_{x} = 1$ : $s_{x} = u_{x}T + \frac{1}{2}a_{x}T^{2} = 108$

questions.question: A particle is projected from the ground with an initial speed of $v$ at an angle θ with horizontal. The average velocity of the particle between its point of projection and highest point of trajectory is?
hints: > Displacement = $\sqrt{(H)^{2} + \left( \frac{R}{2} \right)^{2}}\ $ and time = $T/2$

questions.question: A projectile of mass 2 kg has velocities 3 m/s and 4 m/s at two points during its flight in the uniform gravitational field of the earth. If these two velocities are perpendicular to each other, then find the minimum kinetic energy of the particle during its flight.
questions.conventional:
> Let the angle with horizontal be $\alpha$ and $(90 - \alpha)$ when the velocities are 3 m/s and 4 m/s respectively.

>

> Equating horizontal components: $3\cos \alpha = 4\cos (90 - \alpha)$; $\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4};\cos \alpha = 4/5$

>

> Minimum speed = horizontal component = 3 cos α = 12/5 m/s, so minimum KE = ½ × 2 × (12/5)² = 5.76 J

questions.question: A rifle shoots a bullet with a muzzle velocity of 400 m/s at a small target 400 metre away. The height above the target at which the bullet must be aimed to hit the target is:
questions.conventional:
> Time taken by the bullet to hit the target: 1 s

>

> Vertical displacement during this time interval = 5 m

>

> Hence bullet will hit a point 5 m below the point it is aimed at.

questions.question: A body of mass m is projected horizontally with a velocity v from the top of a tower of height h and it reaches the ground at a distance x from the foot of the tower. If a second body of mass 2 m is projected horizontally from the top of a tower of height 2h, it reaches the ground at a distance 2x from the foot of the tower. Find the horizontal velocity of the second body?
A ball rolls off the top of a staircase with a horizontal velocity of 4.5 m s<sup>–1</sup>. If the steps are 20 cm high and 30 cm broad, then the ball will strike the nth step then $n$?
questions.conventional:
> Time to fall n steps = $\sqrt{\frac{2(0.2n)}{10}} = 0.2\sqrt{n}$; Horizontal distance travelled L = $4.5t = 0.9\sqrt{n}$

>

> It will not clear the nth step if $L < 0.3n$ (the smallest integer value of n);

>

> OR will hit the edge of nth step if $L = 0.3n$

questions.question: ![A projectile launched from A with speed u at 60° to the horizontal lands at B on an incline that rises at 30° from A; C is the point on the ground directly below B.](data/figures/P000238-stem-1.8fe0b4b5.png)Time taken by the projectile to reach from A to B is t. questions.question: ![A projectile launched with speed u from the foot of an incline of 45°, at angle θ to the incline's surface.](data/figures/P000239-stem-1.f44fa4b5.png)A particle is projected from the base of a plane inclined at an angle of $45{^\circ}$ with the horizontal. The initial velocity of projection is $u$ making an angle of $\theta$ with the horizontal as shown. If the particle strikes the inclined plane horizontally, then what is the value of $\tan \theta$?
questions.conventional:
> It strikes the inclined plane at the instant it is at its maximum height;

>

> The angle between the highest point and the point of projection is $45{^\circ}$

>

> Or $\tan 45{^\circ} = 1 = \frac{H_{m}}{\frac{R}{2}} = \frac{u_{y}^{2}}{2g}/(\frac{u_{x}u_{y}}{g})$

questions.question: ![A particle launched with speed u perpendicular to the surface of an incline of angle θ = 37°.](data/figures/P000240-stem-1.d7a7bc24.png)A particle is projected perpendicularly from a long inclined plane as shown. The inclined plane makes an angle $\theta = 37{^\circ}$ with the horizontal. Find the range of the projectile measured along the incline?
questions.conventional:
> Choose down-the-slope as x-axis and $\bot$ up as y-axis:

>

> Then $u_{x} = 0$ and $a_{x} = g\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}g$; $u_{y} = u$ and $a_{y} = - g\cos \theta = - \frac{4}{5}g$

>

> Time of flight T = $\frac{2u_{y}}{a_{y}} = \frac{5u}{2g}$

>

> Range = Displacement along x-axis in time T = $\frac{1}{2}a_{x}T^{2}$

questions.question: ![A projectile launched with speed u from the foot of an incline of angle α = 30°, at θ = 15° above the incline.](data/figures/P000241-stem-1.1438fb9b.png) A plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha = 30{^\circ}$ with respect to the horizontal. A particle is projected with a speed u = 2 m/s from the base of the plane, making an angle of $\theta = 15{^\circ}$ with respect to the plane as shown in the figure. The distance from the base at which the particle hits the plane is close to:
questions.conventional:
> Using normal axes: $\overrightarrow{r_{t}} = u_{x}t\widehat{i} + (u_{y}t - \frac{1}{2}gt^{2})\widehat{j}$ = $\sqrt{2}t\widehat{i} + (\sqrt{2}t - 5t^{2})\widehat{j}$

>

> It will strike the plane at the instant the position vector makes an angle of $30{^\circ}$

>

> $\tan 30{^\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{(\sqrt{2}t - 5t^{2})}{\sqrt{2}t}$
